title: Best gluten-free catering companies in Dubai 2026
body_html:
Best overall for gluten-free home dining in Dubai: myCHEF, a private chef service that agrees the menu with you before the chef ever buys an ingredient. Best for large gluten-free celebrations: full-service event caterers running a dedicated production kitchen. Best for office lunches: drop-off catering specialists with pre-packaged, pre-labelled trays. Best for turnkey venue packages: hotel and restaurant catering arms with a standing gluten-free menu already on the books.

TL;DR
  • myCHEF wins for gluten-free home dining in Dubai because you build the menu with the chef directly, not from a printed card.
  • Full-service event caterers suit large gluten-free parties that need a dedicated production kitchen.
  • Drop-off specialists cover office lunches but rely on written allergen labels, not a chef on site.
  • Hotel and restaurant catering arms offer a tested gluten-free menu with less room to customise.

Why this matters

Gluten intolerance and coeliac disease aren't a preference to hedge around in Dubai's catering scene — a mislabelled dish means a genuinely sick guest, not a minor inconvenience. Getting the format wrong for a gluten-free brief in 2026 usually comes down to one thing: how much control you actually have over the kitchen that touches your food.

A private chef service like myCHEF's private chef and catering service puts you in the room while the menu gets built, which matters more for gluten-free guests than for almost any other dietary flag. This guide compares the four real ways to book gluten-free catering in Dubai — private chef, full-service event catering, drop-off trays and hotel catering — so you can match the format to your guest list and risk tolerance, not just to a menu PDF.

What makes the best gluten-free catering in Dubai

  • Ingredient transparency — you can see or ask about every ingredient before the day, not just read a label at the buffet
  • Separate prep, not just separate plating — cross-contact happens at the chopping board, not the serving tray
  • Genuine menu flexibility — a real gluten-free option on every course, not one token dish
  • Halal alignment — most Dubai households and offices need gluten-free and halal to work together, not as two separate requests
  • Staffing that understands the brief — whoever cooks or plates on the day needs to actually know which dish is gluten-free
  • Scale match — a caterer built for a 200-guest wedding handles a six-person dinner very differently to one built for home dining

A host planning around these six points ends up choosing a format, not just a menu.

Gluten-free catering in Dubai at a glance

Option Best for Standout feature Key limitation
myCHEF (private chef) Home dining with full menu control Menu agreed with the chef before the date Not built for 100+ guest events
Full-service event caterers Large gluten-free celebrations Dedicated production kitchen at scale Menu locked in earlier, less live adjustment
Drop-off catering specialists Office lunches and smaller gatherings Pre-packaged trays with allergen labels No chef on site for last-minute questions
Hotel and restaurant catering arms Turnkey venue packages Standing gluten-free menu already tested Menu fixed to the venue's existing dishes

1. myCHEF: best gluten-free catering for home dining with full menu control

myCHEF is a private chef and catering service that sends a vetted chef to cook in your own kitchen, working from a menu you agree together ahead of the booking. For a gluten-free brief, that means the ingredient list gets discussed at the planning stage, not printed on a card next to a buffet. The same chef format covers dinner parties, weekly meal prep, corporate meals and larger home celebrations, so the gluten-free conversation carries across every occasion.

myCHEF pros:

  • Menu agreed with the chef before the date, so gluten-free swaps happen at the planning stage
  • Cooking happens in your own kitchen, so you can see the ingredients going into each dish
  • Halal-first standards run alongside dietary requests instead of as a separate add-on — see the halal-first catering standards most Dubai households ask for
  • The same format works for a six-person dinner or a larger home celebration

myCHEF cons:

  • Not designed for events running into hundreds of covers
  • Kitchen size and equipment in the home can limit some menu choices
  • Pricing depends on menu and guest count, so it needs a quote rather than a fixed rate card

Best for: households and small offices in Dubai that want a gluten-free menu built around specific guests, not a generic dietary tick-box.

Verdict: book if you want the chef to hear your gluten-free requirements directly, before a single ingredient is bought.

2. Full-service event caterers: best for large gluten-free celebrations

Full-service event caterers in Dubai run a production kitchen away from the venue and plate on site, which becomes useful once a gluten-free guest list runs into the dozens or hundreds. The menu gets fixed further ahead of the date than a private chef booking, because the kitchen is planning a production run rather than a single dinner.

Full-service caterer pros:

  • Handles guest counts a home kitchen can't manage
  • Usually offers a tested gluten-free version of most menu items
  • Staff on site manage service and plating separately from cooking

Full-service caterer cons:

  • Menu locked in earlier, with less room for last-minute changes
  • Less direct contact with the person actually cooking your food
  • Group gluten-free requests get handled as a batch, not a personal brief

Best for: weddings, large birthdays and corporate galas in Dubai where gluten-free is one dietary line among several.

Verdict: consider this format once your guest count passes what a single private chef can cover.

3. Drop-off catering specialists: best for office lunches and smaller gatherings

Drop-off caterers prepare trays off site and deliver without staff, which suits a gluten-free office lunch or a casual home gathering where nobody needs course-by-course plating. The gluten-free tray usually arrives labelled and kept separate from the rest of the order.

Drop-off caterer pros:

  • Lower staffing footprint, useful for weekday office lunches
  • Gluten-free trays typically arrive pre-labelled
  • Faster to book than a fully staffed event

Drop-off caterer cons:

  • No chef on site to answer a last-minute cross-contact question
  • Menu variety is narrower than a bespoke chef menu
  • Reheating and holding times affect texture more than live cooking does

Best for: Dubai offices and casual gatherings where food arrives ready and nobody needs table service.

Verdict: consider for a lunch order; skip for a sit-down celebration.

4. Hotel and restaurant catering arms: best for turnkey venue packages

Hotels and restaurants with a catering arm bring an already-tested gluten-free menu and, often, the venue itself. That's useful when one contract needs to cover food, space and service together, but the gluten-free choices are limited to whatever's already on that kitchen's standing menu.

Hotel catering pros:

  • Menu already tested at volume, so consistency is more predictable
  • Venue and catering can come from a single contract
  • Front-of-house staff usually trained on the venue's own allergen list

Hotel catering cons:

  • Gluten-free choices limited to what's already on the house menu
  • Less flexibility to swap in a specific dish you had in mind
  • The personal menu conversation a private chef offers isn't part of the format

Best for: events already booked into a hotel or restaurant venue, where catering comes bundled with the space.

Verdict: book if the venue is already decided; skip if you're choosing the caterer first.

How we ranked

Each option sits against the six criteria above — ingredient transparency, separate prep, genuine menu flexibility, halal alignment, staffing awareness and scale match. None of the four wins across every scenario; the ranking reflects which gluten-free situation each format actually solves in Dubai in 2026, not a single universal winner.

“The safest gluten-free plan is the one where you set the menu with the chef, not the one where you hope the caterer got it right.”

Which gluten-free caterer should you choose in 2026?

For most households and small offices weighing up gluten-free catering in Dubai, myCHEF is the default starting point: the chef discusses your ingredient list before the booking, and the same relationship covers a one-off dinner or a recurring weekly menu. Move to a full-service event caterer once the guest list passes what one kitchen can manage. Choose a drop-off specialist for a weekday lunch, and let the venue decide if you've already booked a hotel or restaurant space for the event.

Plan your gluten-free menu

FAQ

What's the best gluten-free catering option in Dubai?

For home dining, a private chef service such as myCHEF is the strongest option in 2026 because the menu gets agreed with the chef before ingredients are bought. For events over roughly 50 guests, a full-service caterer with a dedicated production kitchen usually fits better.

Is gluten-free catering in Dubai also halal?

Most households and offices in Dubai need both requirements met together, not as separate requests. Ask any caterer, including a private chef service, whether halal and gluten-free menus are planned as one brief rather than two.

How much does gluten-free catering cost in Dubai?

Cost depends on the menu, guest count and format chosen, so a single figure isn't reliable across private chefs, event caterers, drop-off trays and hotel packages. Get a quote against your actual guest list and menu rather than comparing headline rates.

Can a private chef handle a fully gluten-free dinner party?

Yes — a private chef service builds the menu with you before the date, so gluten-free swaps happen at the planning stage rather than on the night. That control over ingredients is the main advantage over a fixed catering menu.

Do drop-off caterers manage cross-contamination well for gluten-free orders?

Drop-off trays are usually prepared and labelled separately, but there's no chef on site to answer a last-minute question about a specific dish. For higher-risk coeliac guests, a format with direct chef contact carries less uncertainty.

Is gluten-free catering available for corporate events in Dubai?

Yes, most catering formats in Dubai in 2026 — from drop-off lunches to full-service events — can include gluten-free options when the dietary list is shared in advance. Confirm the format handles both the dietary list and the guest count before booking.

One last thing

The detail that catches most hosts out isn't the main course — it's the bread basket, a sauce thickened with flour, or a dessert plated on the same board as a wheat-based cake. Whichever format you book in Dubai this year, ask specifically what touches the gluten-free plate last, not just what's listed in it.

Related guides

  • Drop-off catering options in Dubai
  • Corporate event catering ideas
  • Private chef costs in Dubai
